criteria.evidence: "We will know it is true when each of these checks holds:" "Out: running a review and deciding its findings (the review play, /check-change, owns it)." "When the memory tool cannot reach Phoenix memory, initialize stops and builds nothing, and says the Phoenix install must run on this machine." "Choose the review rule groups (fn-review-rule-groups): records which rule groups of the review fit the project, so a review runs only those and names the groups it skipped."

"A tracker is an outside system, and a write there is visible to the whole team." "A second set of questions for the tracker or the review would ask the person the same things twice." "An empty answer there would look like ... and leave the project with too little memory." "These six jobs share one moment (the project is being set up) and one input (the product owner's answers), so they live in one capability."

"Never: propose an answer without naming its source. A proposal with no source hides a guess, and the person cannot judge it." "Set up the tracker's work-item types (fn-881): finds the tracker the project uses and the types it has, makes each missing type after a typed yes"

"Initialize only records which rule groups fit; the review reads that record and names what it skipped." "A memory block is the set of Phoenix memory files that one setup answer selects, for example the Java standards for a Java answer"

"Today a project gets all of the memory and every review runs every rule, so a project with no database, no front end or no permissions still gets those standards and those findings" "Initialize starts where that install stops, so a project has no Garura memory of its own until initialize runs, and the two never write the same files."
